minutes_text:
INGLEWOOD  CALIFORNIA

  ARTS COMMISSION

The Arts Commission meeting was held on Wednesday, December 9, 2020 via Zoom. Commissioner Battle called
the meeting to order at 6:34 p.m. followed by the flag salute.

Roll Call

  Present
  Commissioner Jacques Lesure, Commissioner at Large
  Commissioner Onna Ehrlich-Bell, District 2
  Commissioner Phyllis Battle, District 3
  Sabrina Barnes, Director, Parks, Recreation and Community Services Department
  Helen Lessick, Public Art Consultant
  Stephanie Maldonado, Senior Management Assistant
  Absent
  Commissioner Aletha Metcalf, District 1
  Commissioner Vicki Banks, District 4

Public Comments

  None

Approval of the Minutes

  Commissioner Lesure made a motion to approve the minutes from October 21, 2020. Commissioner Ehrlich-
Bell seconded and the minutes were approved as follows:

  Ayes: Commissioners Ehrlich-Bell, Battle and Lesure
  Nays: None

Staff Report

  Stephanie Maldonado introduced a staff report recommending the Arts Commission recommend the City
Manager approves the Rogers Park Artist in Residence project agreement, providing a $10,000 artist honorarium and
a $2,000 project materials reimbursement budget, with artist féi hernandez (Pubic Art Fund). Helen Lessick
presented the staff report for the Rogers Park Artist in Residence (RPAIR) project. The project will consist of a
creative services contract with artist féi hernandez for a $10,000 contract for a 12 to 16 week residency, a $2,000
project supply reimbursement and a public art fund match from the Natural Endowment for Arts Grant. féi hernandez
is proposing a project called Intersecting HOPE: Striking Stories of Queer Inglewood residents. The proposal
includes: 10 zoom interviews of individuals representing City of Inglewood’s queer intersectionality, creating a digital
film of those interviewed to be shared online and at Rogers Park’s handball court by appointment, a series of canvas
portraits painted and displayed in the Rogers Park billiards room also viewed by appointment and portraits will be
posted on their website through social media. The budget includes art supplies and payments to interviewees who
share their stories. The RPAiR project’s alternate recommendation is MonaLisa Whitaker. Her project titled,
“Memories of Moments for Inglewood” consists of a collaborative artwork project including 10 to 30 participants of all
  1
   INGLEWOOD  CALIFORNIA

  ARTS COMMISSION

ages who will attend a series of online artmaking sessions and virtual discussions. An online presentation will be
available on a dedicated website, a 5’ x 7’ photo-collage map of Inglewood, individual photo-moments will be affixed
to map and permanently installed at the Community Center. Sabrina Barnes said both projects are really great
however, féi’s project is very creative and innovative as far as the usage of the space and how they will engage with
the community which is the major and ultimate goal of the grant program that is supporting this project.
Commissioner Lesure asked if the project is 16 weeks long. Ms. Lessick stated it is a 12 to 16 week project.
Commissioner Battle mentioned seeing féi perform twice and they were very riveting and brought tears to her eyes.

  Commissioner Ehrlich-Bell made a motion to approve the staff report. Commissioner Lesure seconded and
the staff report was approved as follows:

  Ayes: Commissioners Ehrlich-Bell, Battle and Lesure
  Nays: None

Verbal Reports Regarding the following Public Art Related Projects

Helen Lessick presented a verbal report regarding Arts as Innovation: Embedding Artists and Creativity across Local
Governments in Los Angeles County, by Nahal Jalali. It is an online article that includes the work of artists Michelle
Glass and David Roy who were previously contracted and worked at the Senior Center to conceptualized a cookbook
project utilizing social practice and photography to capture the stories and recipes of community members at the
senior center. The cookbook is entitled Inglewood Heritage Cooking Project and is one of the five (5) projects
highlighted  in  Ms.  Jalali’s  article.  The  article  can  be  viewed  at:
https://d3n8a8pro7vhmx.cloudfront.net/artsforla/pages/9358/attachments/original/1606778659/Art_as_Innovation_Art
s_for_LA_vf2020_Compressed.pdf?1606778659

Public Comments

  None

Commissioners’ Comments/Initiatives/Art Calendar

  Commissioner’s wished each other a Happy Holidays.

Next meeting scheduled for January 20, 2021 at 6:30 p.m. With no further business, the meeting was adjourned at
6:54 p.m.
